title: What a Transaction Is and Why They Go Wrong
coreMove: Map the stimulus and response by ego state so you can see whether the exchange is complementary or crossed.
sourcePressure: Covers transaction as the unit of exchange and the complementary/crossed distinction, with ulterior named only as a forward pointer.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Reducing communication failure to tone or personality instead of tracing which state was addressed and which one replied.

sourceAnchors.name: complementary transaction
sourceAnchors.detail: the source defines it as a response from the ego state addressed, aimed back at the state that sent the original message, allowing conversation to continue
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A complementary transaction is why a plain information request can move quickly: Adult asks, Adult answers, and nothing snaps.

sourceAnchors.name: crossed transaction
sourceAnchors.detail: the source defines it as an unexpected ego-state response that breaks the conversation and makes the exchange go sideways
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A crossed transaction is the moment a factual question receives a scolding answer and the original subject disappears.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: remote software incident Slack thread during a payment outage
exampleSpecs.audience: an engineering lead trying to keep a status request Adult-to-Adult
exampleSpecs.stakes: the outage clock is running and shame will slow the fix
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: James answers the blame-tinged reply with the current rollback status and one needed log line rather than defending the team.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 10:42 a.m., James sees the red incident banner stretch across three monitors.

exampleSpecs.domain: bakery counter refund after a wedding cake pickup error
exampleSpecs.audience: a shop owner hearing a customer's complaint arrive as Adult but feeling pulled into Child apology
exampleSpecs.stakes: a refund conversation can become humiliation or repair
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lea notices that the customer asked for a remedy, not a confession, and replies with options and timing.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "I need to know what you can do before Saturday," the bride says.

exampleSpecs.audience: a PhD candidate answering a professor who treats a scheduling question as defiance
exampleSpecs.stakes: access to the microscope and future trust in the lab
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Andrew waits two beats, then restates the booking question without accepting the Parent-to-Child frame.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The microscope room hums behind a keypad that has locked three students out.

exampleSpecs.audience: a city employee handling residents who want reassurance but ask as accusations
exampleSpecs.stakes: a winter storm queue can turn into mutual contempt
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ingrid hears the caller's Child appeal under the angry phrasing and gives a precise plow estimate without parental correction.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Salt dust marks the cuffs of everyone walking past the service desk.

exampleSpecs.domain: restaurant kitchen allergy ticket during dinner rush
exampleSpecs.audience: a sous-chef catching a server's panicked request before it crosses into accusation
exampleSpecs.stakes: one crossed reply can endanger the diner and split the line staff
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marco repeats the allergen list and asks for the table number instead of answering the server's fear as blame.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You can hear the printer spit another ticket before the server finishes the sentence.

exampleSpecs.audience: a teacher trying to answer a parent's Adult question while the parent's tone invites Parent defense
exampleSpecs.stakes: the student's plan depends on adults not reenacting rank
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Layla sees later that she answered the father's tone instead of his question, then writes the crossed arrows on the conference notes.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Layla until the parking lot to see the cross.

skillTargets: predict why a conversation can continue indefinitely
choose when to recross or wait
avoid introducing ulterior motives too early

tryThisNowSpec: Draw two arrows for the last exchange that went sideways: the arrow you sent, and the arrow you got back. Label the ego states only.
